newsitem.title: USA: Sun outlines plans in Encore storage deal.
newsitem.headline: Sun outlines plans in Encore storage deal.

text.p: Executives of Sun Microsystems Inc's Sun Microsystems Computer Co Friday said they will use storage business assets acquired from Encore Computer Corp to bolster its own revenue growth.
"Our goal is to be one of the top three storage companies in the industry," Ed Zander, president of SMCC, said in a conference call with analysts and media.

Sun announced after the market close on Thursday that it signed a definitive agreement, subject to Encore shareholder approval and regulatory permission, to acquire Encore's storage products, assets and technology for $185 million.
The agreement solidifies a non-binding agreement Encore announced in late May at that valuation.

Kathleen Holmgren, vice president and general manager of SMCC's storage business unit, said the assets include technology involving storage of data from open systems with multiple machines and remote diagnostics capabilities.
A key part of the acquisition is Encore's DataShare software, which enables access to data on mainframes, a market dominated by International Business Machines Corp.

This is a key area where customers will be able to move data to products running the Unix environment, such as Sun's new Starfire server products, from existing mainframes using the Encore technology and products Sun has now acquired.

"We're seing a lot of our customers want to transition data from the mainframe into the open environment," Holmgren said. She said the company expects mainframe-related storage business to be "a key portion" of its storage sales, but to be smaller than its open systems storage business overall.
The executives said they can begin integrating some of the technologies from Encore during the closing process, which Zander said should take 60 to 90 days.
Zander said Sun's data storage business has been growing "substantially" year over year and it aims to be among the top three in the business alongside EMC Corp and IBM.
"We want to give EMC a run for their money," he said. "IBM will always be there."
The executives said the Encore technology will help its systems "coexist" with IBM mainframes in the data centers -- large rooms filled with powerful computers -- of major corporations.
Sun shares closed Friday up 1-11/16 at 25-15/16, while Encore shares gained 0.1875 to 0.96875 in over the counter trading.
